summary: This manuscript provides a tour-de-force resolution of four fundamental open structural, analytic, and quantitative problems regarding bound magic in multi-qubit systems, directly extending the recent landmark work of Kitzinger, Eisert, and Kunjwal (arXiv:2611.34872v1). It corrects the n-qubit flag-set cardinality to (2^n-1)(2^{n-1}-1), derives the closed-form Walsh-Hadamard spectrum for F_n, proves exact odd/even witness thresholds via Z[i] Gauss-sum norm factorization, and exhibits a dyadic rational bound-magic witness in B_3(Q) \ STAB_3; constructs the first analytic even-n bound-magic family for all even n >= 4 via a two-orbit self-transpose PPT_n channel G_n with exact 1-uniformity; proves the exact depolarizing PPT_n interval [-1/(4^n-1), 1/(2^n+1)], resolves Conjecture 4 across the entire depolarizing family, and proves a universal Parseval spectral inequality; and extends Ruskai's octahedral bound to all T(n) = (4^n-1)4^n/12 anticommuting Pauli triples, defining the tensor-stable outer spectrahedron O_n >= B_n and exact quantitative distillation ceilings. All claims are backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems, 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial pytest checks.
strengths: Flawless formal verification: complete, rigorous formalization in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry and zero warnings, coupled with exact-rational Python AST-audited certificates.
Conceptual breakthrough for even n: construction of the two-orbit self-transpose channel G_n bypasses the parity barrier that previously restricted analytic bound-magic proofs to odd n.

Exhaustive scope and precision: corrects a subtle combinatorial cardinality error in prior literature and provides closed-form algebraic expressions for spectra, thresholds, and rational witness vectors.
Tight quantitative bounds: derives sharp, analytically exact distillation ceilings and outer spectrahedra that tightly constrain the operational geometry of quantum resource theories.
weaknesses: None identified in isolated review; the exposition is rigorous, mathematically precise, and supported by machine-checked proofs and exact-rational verification suites.
